stem:
A student investigates light from different galaxies.

Fig. 2.1 shows the lines in the absorption spectrum from a distant galaxy.

[[fig:f1]]

The wavelength of one of the lines in the absorption spectrum is *λ*. The wavelength of this spectral line in the laboratory is *λ*₀.

The observations of the same spectral line are repeated for different galaxies.

The student determines the distance *d* of each galaxy from the Earth.

It is suggested that *λ* and *d* are related by the equation

$\frac{λ − λ₀}{λ₀} = \frac{Hd}{c}$

where *c* is the speed of light in free space and *H* is the Hubble constant.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A graph is plotted of *λ* on the y-axis against $\frac{d}{c}$ on the x-axis.

Determine expressions for the gradient and y-intercept.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Values of *d* and *λ* are given in Table 2.1.

[[fig:f2]]

The value of *c* is 3.00 × 10⁵ km s⁻¹.

Calculate and record values of $\frac{d}{c} / 10^{15}\,\mathrm{s}$ in Table 2.1. Include the absolute uncertainties in $\frac{d}{c}$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Plot a graph of *λ* / nm against $\frac{d}{c} / 10^{15}\,\mathrm{s}$. Include error bars for $\frac{d}{c}$.

[[fig:f3]]

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Draw the straight line of best fit and a worst acceptable straight line on your graph. Label both lines.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Determine the gradient of the line of best fit. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text: Determine the y-intercept of the line of best fit. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Using your answers to (a), (c)(iii) and (c)(iv), determine the values of *λ*₀ and *H*. Include appropriate units.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Hubble’s law suggests that the age *T* of the universe is related to *H* by

$T = \frac{1}{H}$.

Determine a value for *T*. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

figures.caption: Fig. 2.1
figures.alt: An absorption spectrum with several dark lines, an arrow indicating wavelength λ, and an arrow showing increasing wavelength.

figures.caption: Table 2.1
figures.alt: A three-column table with headings for distance d, d/c, and wavelength λ, containing six rows of distance and wavelength values and blank cells for d/c.
A blank graph grid with λ / nm on the vertical axis and d/c / 10¹⁵ s on the horizontal axis.
